data.body: /cc @Zales0123 Can you have a look? Maybe we should go with the select for these templates, choices populated via parameter.

This is really blocking and is really is less powerful. Why did this configuration go in the UI in the first place ? Another problem is that now administrators can easily wreak havoc if they fiddle with the values in the backend, whereas before the payment configuration was far safer as it was out of reach for admin users to modify..
And more : a password stored **in plain text** in the DB.

@tchapi You are right and I really appreciate the feedback you are giving us, but your demanding attitude is really demotivating, at least to me. So, when you some good idea or remark (and seems like you do), please put in a bit nicer set of words or even better, a PR. Thanks.

@makasim What do you think about security issue raised here, with the GatewayConfig?

@pjedrzejewski I'm trying, but understand that sometimes all the BC breaks are really demotivating too, on our side. It's hard to keep up with the project - don't forget we don't have the full view like you have on the master plan for the Sylius releases, just a few blog posts; and the breaking PRs come, and we try our best to accomodate our code so that we can get the bug fixes and still use Sylius in production _because we love the framework and want to stick to it_. My apologies anyway for the attitude, I'll behave — word.

@inssein Thank you very much for your feedback, it's really helpful :) Yes, managing payment gateways in UI is a big change, the main reason for that was to allow administrator to configure multiple paypal/stripe/etc. accounts for gateways without the need to change a code. We'll definitely process about them and consider your suggestions to make this feature as much useful and secure as it can be, as fast as we can do it.

I am not sure I understand the enc problem . 

Why these values have to be encrypted? 
What can an attacker do with them? 

Maybe I miss something. 

No need to overwrite DynamicRegistry. It is possible to provide a "custom" storage for gateway configs (which could be a decorator for real one) which takes care of encryption stuff.
@makasim If he knows these, for example PayPal credentials of your merchant account, he can charge on your behalf, am I right? :/
@pjedrzejewski but money goes to your merchant account. What's the point?

One case that I see for one is possibility to "hack" notification process. If you know the secret you can sign a exploite request with the correct hash. That's why Payum uses token for every payment. 
As long as you use them you are safe even if the secret is stolen.
Also if an attacker was able to get into your database it is most likely he has an access to your code and can edit it, and can get secret data there. or from parameters.yml if it is stored there.
@inssein WDYT? @makasim Do you know if other eCommerce solutions encrypt these? I recall some do.
JMSPaymentBundle does it.
@inssein Your arguments makes sense to me. It would be good to have such storage in Payum.

@pjedrzejewski @Zales0123 while you guys figure out the encryption issue, could I get some pointers on to how Sylius would address the issue of not being able to override specific code-related variables?

I was thinking maybe a decorator, like so: (not including the implementation of the storage for brevity, but it just array merges the last argument).
```
  app.gateway.storage:
    class: AppBundle\GatewayStorage
    decorates: payum.dynamic_gateways.config_storage
    arguments:
      - "@app.gateway.storage.inner"
      - stripe_checkout:
          payum.template.obtain_token: "@@SyliusShop/Payum/Action/obtainCheckoutToken.html.twig"
          payum.action.convert_payment: "@@app.payum.action.convert_payment"
    public: false
    decoration_priority: 128
```
Note: Not sure why sylius chose to fetch the gateway by name (which doesn't even show up in admin as its translatable) instead of something like the code.

The above works, but seems like there could be an easier way...

**References:**
 - Payum/Payum#634 (issue on Payum about encrypting gateway configuration)
 - Payum/Payum#635 (PR for Payum, introducing encrypted storage)
 - Payum/PayumBundle#414 (PR for PayumBundle, introducing encryption configuration to the bundle)
 - #7721 (PR for Sylius, handling encryption in form types)

What is currently recommended way to override parameters like `payum.template.obtain_token` without putting them into UI via form extesion, like what was asked in initial question of the issue?

Seems to be point of intereset for other people as well  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56194992/how-can-i-customize-stripe-template-in-sylius
I've went with @inssein decorator for `DoctrineStorage` to 'array_merge' my extra parameters with `GatewayConfig` parameters. Thank you, Hussein.

> 
> Maybe we can add a new feature to `SyliusPayumBundle` to handle this kind of specific overrides, something based on a `sylius_payum` config for exemple.

Yes, please!

It's a headache to change Stripe checkout layout... :(
